speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sit. A shilling. Roast mutton, and a cup of Rhenish. That is the supper.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: A shilling is a fortune when a man has eaten nothing since Friday and talked through everything between. Tapster.

speaker: (the tapster)
text: Mutton, and the Rhenish.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Gabriel Harvey will not die, and he will not stop printing. I have a quarrel with a man who manages both at once, which is to say he manages neither.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Print is a long life. Eat while the mutton is hot.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I will eat, and I will not forgive him for the eating. He writes as if the page were a pulpit and the pulpit a shop.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One shilling covers the mutton and the cup. I am not opening a second quarrel with the price.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Then hear a smaller one. A sleeping alderman, dreaming of his thumb-rings. He turns the hand so the stones catch a light that is not in the room.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thumb-rings. I have the picture. You may leave him asleep.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I will not leave him. Out of my own book of the night, the little things come with him. So small they are almost nothing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Almost nothing still takes a long time, in your mouth.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Spokes of a gnat's wagon. That is the size. A wagon, and the spokes of it, and the gnat who thinks he drives.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A wagon. Go on. I am hearing it. I am not writing it down at the table.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: A spinner's legs. Blisters on a lady's lip, put there by some imp for spite. You could lose the whole nation of them in a crease of the napkin.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The alderman would pay to hear them described. You are enjoying him.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I am enjoying the size. Men write devils the height of a house because they cannot draw a thing small enough to lose.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Harvey is still in the first part of the hour. You have not finished with him.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I never finish with him. He will not die, so I am not obliged to. He prints, and I answer, and the answer is the only economy I have.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Eat the mutton. The shilling is already the supper. Anger keeps poorly in a hot room.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: The cup is a cup. I have had worse, and I have paid nothing for this one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One cup with the mutton. I know the length of your second hour. I am not afraid of it yet.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: Then sit further in. The alderman has turned his hand again. The thumb-ring is the only idea he has ever completed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let him keep it. I have the spokes, and the legs, and the blisters. That is as small as I can hold at one sitting.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: You hold more than you admit. You have the face of a man who has already taken the wagon home in his ear.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have not taken it anywhere. Eat.

speaker: thomas_nashe
text: I will eat. Harvey may live through the mutton. He has lived through worse answers than mine.
